ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Sandal money is the expense of travelling on foot in straw sandals.
EvidenceBody: In the Huangbo–Nanquan exchange, Nanquan sets gruel-water money aside and asks who will repay the sandal money; later records say a reply saves sandal money or warn against wasting it. Chan turns ordinary travel expense into an account of whether a journey or visit was worth its cost. The Record of Master Zhe’an Fan preserves his warning that someone who lightly throws away good time does not even value sandal money.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The explicit repayment, saving, and wasting predicates make travel expense an encounter reckoning.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The famous repayment question is Nanquan’s utterance inside the Huangbo case, not Huangbo’s; later quotations must preserve that turn.
